chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

Indeed, in 'Ali (عليه السلام) is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of a thousand Prophets from among the Prophets, and indeed the knowledge that descended with Adam (عليه السلام) was not raised, and no knowledgeable one dies such that his knowledge goes away; rather, knowledge is inherited.

key_terms.أَلْفِ نَبِيٍّ: a thousand Prophets, indicating vast prophetic qualities or legacies
key_terms.سُنَّةَ: the prophetic way, pattern, or tradition embodied in practice
key_terms.عَالِمٌ: a knowledgeable one or possessor of sacred knowledge
key_terms.لَمْ يُرْفَعْ: was not taken away or removed
key_terms.نَزَلَ: descended, indicating revelation or divinely bestowed knowledge
key_terms.يُتَوَارَثُ: is inherited or passed down successively

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Imam 'Ali's relation to the Prophets and the inheritance of divine knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the immense spiritual and epistemic rank of Imam 'Ali (عليه السلام), linking him to the legacy of the Prophets. It teaches that divine knowledge bestowed from the time of Adam (عليه السلام) remains preserved and is transmitted through inheritance rather than being lost with the death of a knower.
